provider_if_inherited: Client A; Client B; SaaS providers
implementation_statement: The owner holds every account inside the boundary: the email and file suite (owner only), the accounting SaaS (owner plus the tax accountant's read-only user), and the owner's named accounts on Client A's portal and gateway and Client B's platform, which the clients create and remove. Gap: no written list of accounts and no periodic review of who can reach each one.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control via CSCA-A (3)); GRS-B (1)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-engineer is the only engineer and the independent consultant of record, so duties cannot be separated inside the business. Client A acts as the second person for its systems: it enables each gateway window, the gateway gives view-only access, and Client A reviews the session logs weekly; the owner answers that review within one business day (POL-01 6.4 and 6.5). The tax accountant has read-only access to the accounting SaaS. Gap: the owner keeps no own session log to compare with Client A's review until 2026-10-31 (POAM-009).
evidence: Client A weekly session review; POL-01 6.4 and 6.5; POAM-009

implementation_statement: The owner works in the laptop's administrator account every day, including email, web, and client gateway sessions. A standard daily account will be created and the administrator account kept for installs only by 2026-09-30.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control, approved use, via CSCA-A (3))

implementation_statement: Laptop locks after 5 minutes idle; phone and tablet after 1 minute. Unlock needs the password, PIN, or biometric.

Client A operates the gateway: named account, MFA, view-only roles, sessions enabled only for review windows, and its own session logging. Owner responsibility: connect only from a business-only device and network and never store the gateway credentials. Gap: sessions ran from the mixed-use administrator laptop over the shared home Wi-Fi, and the browser saved the gateway password.
evidence: Client A gateway enablement emails; browser password store (P07 test)
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a remote and third-party connections; Form 3 Q12a-12b; via CSCA-A (3))

implementation_statement: Phone and tablet use passcodes and device encryption and can be wiped remotely. Gap: the phone camera roll syncs field photos of gate controls and security features to a personal consumer photo cloud.

The owner completed Client A's security awareness module on 2026-06-05, as CSCA-A (5) requires before access. Gap: no other security training, and nothing on information-stealing malware or CEII handling. A short annual course is planned by 2026-11-30.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Client A logs gateway sessions and reviews them weekly. The owner keeps no log of the owner's own sessions to compare with Client A's review, and never looks at the suite's sign-in history. From 2026-10 the owner logs each gateway session and checks the suite sign-in history on the first working day of each month.

provider_if_inherited: Client A (gateway session logs); suite provider
implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-engineer is the only administrator, so the audit records relied on are kept by others. Client A logs and reviews every gateway session, and the suite provider keeps the sign-in history. Neither is a file the owner keeps. The owner reviews the suite sign-in history monthly (POL-01 7.8).
evidence: Client A session review; suite sign-in history; POL-01 7.8

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-engineer designed, operates, and assessed the controls, and P07 states that independence is limited. The IT technician helped run the tests under an NDA but also supports the laptop, and no client staff took part. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the business, such as the IT technician under NDA or a peer engineer, at least every second year. Client A may ask to see the POA&M items tied to CSCA-A. The suite provider's SOC 2 report (P09) covers inherited controls. Base CA-2 is the July self-assessment.

Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board and the business develops no software. SaaS changes are the providers', covered by their SOC 2 reports. Under CM-3(g) the change control element for the owner's own setting changes is the security log, where they are recorded (P09 CC8.1).
evidence: Suite provider SOC 2 report (P09); security log; P09 CC8.1

implementation_statement: The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no peer engineer arrangement and no sealed emergency sheet (due 2026-12-31).

Synced project folders are kept by the suite with 30 days of version history (inherited). Owner responsibility: model files, software configuration, and the CEII archive stay on the laptop and are copied only to a monthly USB backup that is not encrypted and has never been restored.
evidence: Suite settings; USB drive check (P07 test)
regulatory_driver: 18 CFR 12.35(a) (consultant must keep a full understanding of the record); CSCA-A (1)

implementation_statement: The suite administrator account (the owner's) requires a password and an authenticator app code. Recovery codes are printed and kept in the locked cabinet.

provider_if_inherited: Accounting SaaS provider; Client B platform vendor; Client A
implementation_statement: Client A enforces MFA on its portal and gateway. Gap: MFA is available but off on the accounting SaaS and on the owner's Client B platform account (GRS-B (2) requires it). Owner turns both on by 2026-09-15.
Passwords are saved in the laptop browser, including the Client A gateway password, and two passwords are reused. A password manager with unique passphrases replaces the browser store by 2026-09-15.

The owner's digital signing certificate, used to seal reports, sits in the laptop's certificate store, unlocked by the daily administrator login. It will move to a hardware token with its own PIN by 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: 18 CFR 12.36(h) (report signed and sealed by the independent consultant)

implementation_statement: No written procedure existed for the 24-hour notices in CSCA-A (7) and GRS-B (3) or for reporting an unauthorized CEII disclosure to FERC. The P08 notification matrix and printed contact sheet set them; walkthrough due 2026-09-30.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A 4.2 via CSCA-A (7)); C-DAMS-R02 (client's 12.10 duty); 18 CFR 388.113(h)(2)

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook for unauthorized access through the client gateway account was adopted on 2026-08-31. Gap: not yet walked through with the IT technician (due 2026-09-30).
Paper is kept in a locked file cabinet. Gap: the USB backup drive with CEII sits unencrypted on the desk, and a former client's printed drawings from 2025 are still in the cabinet.
regulatory_driver: 18 CFR 388.113(h)(2) (secure place); C-DAMS-R01 (Form 1 Q22 via CSCA-A (1))

implementation_statement: Paper is cross-cut shredded. Gap: no procedure or record for returning or destroying client material at the end of an engagement, and no certificate for the former client's 2025 drawings.
The home office door locks and the file cabinet is locked when the owner is away. Household members do not use the office equipment.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every July and after a new client, system, or incident.

The suite provider's SOC 2 report was reviewed on 2026-07-23 (P09). Gap: no vendor list; the AI anomaly detection SaaS received Client B data under click-through terms; the personal photo cloud holds field photos; the field assistant has no agreement.
regulatory_driver: GRS-B (1); C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a roles with third-party contractors via CSCA-A (9))

implementation_statement: The laptop's host firewall is on and the router updates itself. Gap: the home Wi-Fi is shared with household devices and a smart TV. A separate business network is planned by 2026-10-31; the phone hotspot is used for gateway sessions until then.

provider_if_inherited: SaaS providers; Client A; Client B
implementation_statement: Every SaaS service, the Client A portal and gateway, and the Client B platform use TLS. Client documents are exchanged only through the clients' portals or the suite, not by ordinary email attachments.

Laptop full-disk encryption on since 2025-02; phone and tablet encrypted; the CEII archive is an encrypted container; the suite encrypts stored data (inherited). Gap: the USB backup drive is not encrypted.
Automatic updates are on for the laptop, phone, tablet, and router. SaaS providers patch their services. Engineering software is updated when the vendor releases a version.
The built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on, install software only from vendor sites, and act on alerts.
